correctness.rationale: The exact zero/one counts have a Poisson weak limit and a concentrated mean respectively. Exact pgf remainder expectations give two different scales for numerator and denominator. Conditioning on each positive zero count yields the reciprocal atom; conditioning on zero yields the divergent branch. The delta-method bias and variance are reconstructed from the Poisson covariance matrix and independently checked by finite Poisson summation, and the 5% rejection atoms are separated strictly from both limit critical boundaries. The proof is complete for the stated triangular arrays; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The two closest open-access primary sources define this exact ratio, weight family, and fixed-parameter Gaussian calibration, and warn of possible degeneracy, but do not derive the joint increasing-mean/boundary-weight reciprocal-Poisson null limit or the 36.79% size. Actual mathematical-record searches and own prior-claim comparisons identified no theorem that directly implies the final claim. Generic reciprocal rare-count asymptotics remain a disclosed historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Generic reciprocal-of-rare-count asymptotics may imply abstract pieces of this limit after a nontrivial identification of the statistic; a definitive historical-priority claim is not made.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a specific, nontrivial nonuniformity in the normal calibration of a published goodness-of-fit method: an exactly Poisson null has limiting 36.79% rejection at nominal 5% under a mathematically natural rare-zero/boundary-weight scaling. The sharp atom-at-infinity description identifies the cause and distinguishes it from ordinary fixed-mean small-sample error. It does not make a recommendation to use the stressed tuning in practice.
